subject.title: CLI startup preflight can corrupt the live state DB while a gateway is running — health-check commands caused "database disk image is malformed" (2026.6.6, macOS); vanilla SQLite control does NOT reproduce

question: Should non-gateway CLI/status/doctor access to the shared state DB become RPC-first with read-only/no-maintenance fallback, a gateway-owned single-writer lease, or both?
rationale: Source confirms mutable CLI-side DB open/checkpoint paths, but the durable fix changes ownership across gateway RPC observability, doctor migrations, plugin-state probes, operator recovery, and upgrade behavior.

options.title: RPC-first plus no-maintenance fallback
options.body: Status, health, and stability use the running gateway first, and file fallback while a gateway owns the DB is read-only with no journal or checkpoint pragmas.

options.title: Gateway single-writer lease
options.body: The gateway owns the shared DB write and maintenance lease, and non-gateway processes fail closed or route through gateway APIs for writes and maintenance.

options.title: Forensic harness first
options.body: Pause implementation until the reporter's bundle or a native runtime stress harness confirms the exact helper/runtime interaction before selecting the policy.

recommendation.title: RPC-first plus no-maintenance fallback
recommendation.body: Status, health, and stability use the running gateway first, and file fallback while a gateway owns the DB is read-only with no journal or checkpoint pragmas.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision cuts across the DB-first runtime-state architecture and gateway/CLI ownership boundaries introduced by the broad SQLite refactor.
